Taylor: Hi team, quick Q: I updated marital status and moved to AZ (community property). Want to add spouse as 401(k) beneficiary and bump HSA to family. Anything special because of the state change or my outstanding 401k loan?
Maya (Benefits): Congrats! :tada: You need to submit the 401(k) beneficiary form and the HSA beneficiary form. In community property states we usually require spouse consent if you name someone other than spouse. If you're naming spouse as primary, standard form is fine.
Taylor: Link to the forms? Any vendor turnaround time?
Maya (Benefits): https://benefits.redwood.com/forms/beneficiary-update.pdf. Vendor (BrightPlan) processing is typically 3-7 business days after we submit. If you want faster processing, attach marriage cert and a signed spouse consent (if applicable) when you submit.
Rae (Payroll): Payroll cutoff for contribution changes to affect next paycheck is the 25th 11:59pm PT. If you miss it, change applies the following cycle. Include note `BEN-HSA-FAM` in PayPortal comments so we flag it.
Taylor: My 401(k) loan  if I change payroll deductions or go on leave, could that trigger loan default/acceleration?
Sam (Total Rewards): Good question. Loan repayment schedules continue unless you terminate employment. Short leaves don't generally trigger acceleration. However unpaid LOAs over 6 months sometimes require plan admin review. If separation occurs, outstanding loan balance may be due or treated as distribution per plan docs. We recommend not reducing payments to zero unless necessary.
Taylor: If I want to roll my old 401k from previous employer into Redwood plan later, is spouse consent required for rollovers?
Maya (Benefits): Rollovers into your account don't require spouse consent. Spousal rules apply to beneficiary/designation and in some cases QDROs for divorces.
Taylor: HSA family limit question: do I need to re-enroll or will benefits auto-update?
Maya (Benefits): You need to change HSA election in PayPortal > Benefits > HSA to select family coverage. We will adjust per-paycheck deduction to meet family max if you choose that option. Confirm before the payroll cutoff.
Taylor: Any tax impact I should be aware of during year of marriage (withholding)?
Rae (Payroll): Changing to Roth contributions increases taxable wages; switching HSA from single to family does not change taxable wages (HSA contributions are pre-tax). If you change marital filing status in Workday/HR, that may affect payroll withholding — use the tax withholding estimator in PayPortal or file a new W-4.
Benefits Bot: Ticket created #BEN-9001. Forms queued for review.
Taylor: Thanks all. I'll upload marriage cert and fill forms tonight and submit the HSA election before the 25th.
Maya (Benefits): Ping us if you want help completing the PDF.
Sam (Total Rewards): One more note: if you later take a domestic partner benefit instead of spouse, vendor requirements differ. Ask before switching.
Rae (Payroll): Noted. We'll watch for `BEN-HSA-FAM` in the notes.
Taylor: Appreciated :thumbsup:
